resources.string: Open Metrora on your computer and scan the QR code to get started.
Scan a Metrora Desktop QR code
Find your computer on the local network.
Local and private · No account required
Your data stays on your devices.
Need help? Open the pairing guide on Desktop.
You’ll find the QR code in the Connect section.
Compare the code and approve the connection on Desktop.
The pairing request is now visible on Desktop. Compare the code below with the one shown there.
The code confirms the Desktop identity before the connection is approved.
After the codes match, tap Codes match here and approve this phone on your computer.
Loading the pairing saved on this phone.
Use the local IP or hostname shown by Desktop, without https://.
Add your Metrora Desktop computer to see a usage overview on this phone.
Checking the computer address you entered.
A pairing request is ready on Desktop. Compare the six-digit code before approval.
The codes matched on both devices. Approve this phone on Desktop.
Desktop is reachable and this overview is current.
Keep Metrora Desktop available on the local network.
Showing the last saved overview. Refresh to check Desktop for newer data.
Pairing succeeded, but the first usage overview is not available yet. Refresh to try again.
Your saved overview is still available. Try again when Desktop is on the same network.
No overview is saved yet. Try Refresh when Desktop is available.
This phone is no longer authorized by Desktop. Pair it again when Desktop is available.
Metrora found local state that is not safe to use automatically. Remove it locally and pair again.
Your saved data is kept when possible. Follow the message below and try again.
Saved on this phone · refresh failed
Desktop did not provide cost aggregates for this period.
Desktop did not provide model rows for this period.
Your computer is paired. Refresh to load the first overview from Desktop.
There is no saved overview to show yet. Try Refresh when Desktop is available.
Metadata-only Activity. Prompts, responses, code, tool arguments and private paths stay on Desktop.
No bounded session rows are available for this Project and period.
This Desktop does not advertise a compatible Sessions projection. Home and Usage remain available when supported.
This Desktop does not advertise a compatible Models projection for the selected Project scope.
Partial historical model detail. Rows shown are available evidence, not a total for the full period.
Model detail is unavailable for this Project and period. Cost, calls and sessions remain separate accounting facts.
This Desktop did not provide a bounded Spend projection for the selected Project scope.
Workspace remains a Desktop/core identity and evidence boundary. No bounded mobile projection is advertised in Foundation V1.
This companion surface is not available yet. No placeholder data is shown.
Point your camera at the QR code shown in Metrora on your computer.
That QR code is not a Metrora Desktop connection.
Metrora will verify the computer and show a six-digit code before Desktop access is approved.
Keep both devices on the same network.
Metrora connects directly to Desktop. No account or cloud relay is used.
Camera access is needed to scan
Metrora uses the camera only to read a Desktop connection QR code.
This phone connects directly to Metrora Desktop on your local network. No cloud account is used.
This asks Desktop to remove this phone, then clears the local pairing after Desktop confirms.
This only removes local credentials and cached data. It does not revoke the old credential on Desktop.
Remove local pairing and pair again
Desktop must confirm the revocation before Metrora clears the local pairing. If Desktop is unavailable, nothing is claimed as revoked.
This clears the pairing credential and saved usage from this phone only. The old device may remain known to Desktop.
This clears the unreadable or inconsistent local pairing record from this phone. It does not change Desktop.
Pairing complete. Usage is now up to date.
The phone is paired, but the first usage snapshot is not available yet.
The pairing and cached usage were removed from this phone only.
Desktop confirmed revocation and local pairing data was removed.
Desktop confirmed revocation, but local cleanup still needs attention.
The unreadable cached snapshot was removed. The pairing is still valid.
Could not connect to this computer
Enter a computer address such as 192.168.1.24 or metrora-pc.local.
Enter a port between 1 and 65535. Metrora Desktop usually uses 7777.
Metrora Desktop could not be reached. Check that sharing is on and both devices are on the same network.
Desktop did not respond in time. Check the network and try again.
That address is not a Metrora Desktop endpoint.
This Desktop does not expose the companion API required by this phone.
Update Metrora Desktop before pairing this phone.
Desktop is not accepting new phone pairings right now.
Desktop declined the request or the approval expired. Start again when you are ready.
Desktop already knows this phone. Try pairing again, or remove the old local pairing first.
The Desktop identity could not be verified. Check the address and do not approve an unexpected computer.
The Desktop identity changed during pairing. Start again only if you recognise the computer.
The secure identity for this phone changed. Pair the computer again to create a new trusted relationship.
The confirmation code did not match. Do not approve this pairing; start again.
Desktop no longer accepts this phone pairing. Pair again when Desktop is available.
Desktop did not confirm revocation. Access was not claimed as revoked; retry or forget only on this phone.
Desktop returned data this version of Metrora could not verify. Try again, and update Desktop if it continues.
Metrora could not safely use some local data. The secure pairing was kept when possible.
Local pairing needs recovery before it can be used again.
Metrora could not complete that action. Try again.
Security detail is available below. Do not approve a pairing when the code or computer identity is unexpected.
